title: Sampling Theory — structured question bank
provenance: Two exact June 2026 Paper 2 PYQs transcribed from the repository's pyq_j26_full.json. All other prompts are author-created revision prompts, not official PYQs. The official PYQ answers and candidate responses are preserved separately.

topics.name: Horvitz–Thompson and varying probability sampling
questions: What is the first-order inclusion probability πᵢ?
The probability that unit i is included in the sample.
What is the Horvitz–Thompson contribution of a sampled unit?
yᵢ/πᵢ.
State the HT estimator of a finite-population total.
Ŷ_HT=Σᵢ∈s yᵢ/πᵢ.
Why is the HT total design-unbiased?
Because Eₚ(Iᵢ)=πᵢ, so Eₚ(ΣIᵢyᵢ/πᵢ)=Σyᵢ.
What condition is required for every target unit?
πᵢ>0.
What is the second-order inclusion probability?
πᵢⱼ=P(i and j are both included).

topics.name: Stratified sampling and allocation
questions: What is a stratum?
A non-overlapping population subgroup sampled separately.
State the stratified estimator of the population total.
Ŷ_st=Σ_h N_h ȳ_h.
State the variance under independent SRSWOR within strata.
V(ȳ_st)=Σ_h W_h²(1−f_h)S_h²/n_h.
What is proportional allocation?
n_h=n(N_h/N).
What is Neyman allocation for equal unit costs?
n_h proportional to N_h S_h.
When is stratification especially useful?
When strata are internally homogeneous and differ from one another.

topics.name: Ratio and regression estimators
questions: Define the ratio estimator of a population mean.
ȳ_R=ȳ_s( X̄/ x̄_s), using known population auxiliary mean X̄.
What is the ratio estimator of a total?
Ŷ_R= X̄·N·(ȳ_s/x̄_s), equivalently X̄_total·(ȳ_s/x̄_s).
What is the key assumption behind a ratio relationship?
A regression through or near the origin is a useful approximation.
State the regression estimator of a mean.
ȳ_reg=ȳ_s+b(X̄−x̄_s).
When can ratio estimation improve precision?
When study and auxiliary variables are positively correlated and the ratio model is suitable.
Why can ratio estimators be biased?
They are nonlinear functions involving a random sample denominator.

topics.name: Cluster sampling
questions: What is a cluster?
A group of population elements treated as a sampling unit at the first stage.
What is one-stage cluster sampling?
Select clusters and observe every element in selected clusters.
What is two-stage cluster sampling?
Select clusters, then sample elements within selected clusters.
What is the main practical advantage of cluster sampling?
Reduced travel, listing and fieldwork costs.
What is the usual variance effect of positive within-cluster similarity?
It increases variance relative to an equally sized SRS.
Define the design effect.
Variance under the complex design divided by variance under SRS of the same nominal size.

topics.name: Systematic sampling
questions: How is a systematic sample selected?
Choose a random start and then select every k-th unit.
What is the interval for N units and sample size n when N/n is integral?
k=N/n.
What is a random start?
A uniformly selected starting position among the k possible positions.
What is the main risk of systematic sampling?
Periodicity in the ordered list can align with the sampling interval.
Can a single systematic sample estimate its own design variance without extra assumptions?
Generally no; one random start gives limited direct variance information.
Why is ordering the frame important?
It can create implicit stratification or harmful periodic patterns.

topics.name: PPS schemes and their estimators
questions: What does PPS mean?
Probability proportional to size.
Which measure determines selection probability in PPS?
A known size measure attached to each sampling unit.
When is PPS useful?
When unit sizes vary substantially and size is related to the study variable.
What is PPS with replacement commonly paired with?
The Hansen–Hurwitz estimator.
What is PPS without replacement commonly associated with?
Horvitz–Thompson estimation using unit inclusion probabilities.
Why must certainty units be handled carefully?
Their inclusion probability is one and they are included with certainty.

topics.name: Two-stage, multi-stage and double sampling
questions: What happens in two-stage sampling?
Primary units are selected first, then secondary units within them.
What is multi-stage sampling?
Sampling proceeds through more than two nested stages.
What is double sampling also called?
Two-phase sampling.
How does two-phase sampling differ from two-stage sampling?
Two-phase sampling collects auxiliary information in phase one and detailed information in phase two; stages select nested units.
Give an example of a primary sampling unit.
A village or census block.
Why are stage-specific probabilities multiplied?
The overall inclusion probability follows the conditional selection probabilities across stages.

topics.name: Non-sampling errors
questions: What is coverage error?
Mismatch between the target population and the sampling frame.
What is nonresponse error?
Error arising when selected units do not provide the required data.
What is measurement error?
Difference between the recorded response and the true characteristic.
Can a census suffer non-sampling error?
Yes; a census can have coverage, nonresponse, processing and measurement errors.
What is response bias?
Systematic distortion in answers or reporting.
Name one way to reduce interviewer-related error.
Standardised training, neutral wording and field supervision.

topics.name: Nonnegative variance estimation, ordered and unordered estimators
questions: What is an ordered estimator?
An estimator whose form depends on the order or sequence in which sample units are represented.
What is an unordered estimator?
An estimator invariant to permutations of the sample-unit labels/order.
Does an unbiased estimator have to be nonnegative for every sample?
No; unbiasedness is an expectation property.
Can the true variance be negative?
No; variance is nonnegative.
Why can an unbiased variance estimator be negative?
Its realised sample expression may be negative even though its design expectation equals the true variance.
What should be distinguished in a variance question?
The true variance, an unbiased estimator of it, and a nonnegative alternative estimator.

officialPyqs.stem: Study the following statements regarding the Horvitz–Thompson estimator: A. Horvitz–Thompson estimate is an ordered estimate. B. The unbiased estimate of the variance of the Horvitz–Thompson estimator does not reduce to zero when all population values are equal. C. The unbiased estimate of the variance of the Horvitz–Thompson estimator may assume negative values for some samples. D. Horvitz–Thompson estimator is a biased estimator.
